claims.text: The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy has a lamellar duplex microstructure.
The duplex structure consists of a soft FCC phase and a hard BCC/B2 or intermetallic phase.
The as-cast microstructure is coarse and has limited interfacial density.
Cryogenic rolling followed by controlled annealing can transform the cast lamellar structure into a hierarchical ultrafine-grained duplex architecture.
Cryogenic rolling introduces severe plastic deformation.
Controlled annealing induces nanoscale grain refinement and phase decomposition.
The processed architecture contains a nanoscale FCC matrix interspersed with fine, coherent hard-phase precipitates.
The processing increases the density of coherent phase boundaries.
The increased phase-boundary density blocks dislocation motion and raises strength.
Hierarchical structural heterogeneity creates a constraint effect that improves mechanical response.
The refined architecture creates strain gradients that promote uniform plastic flow.
The processed architecture promotes microcrack arrest.
Cryogenic rolling and annealing should increase yield strength by approximately 20% or more relative to the as-cast alloy.
Cryogenic rolling and annealing should maintain or increase elongation relative to the as-cast alloy.
The treatment can break the conventional strength–ductility trade-off.
The as-cast baseline typically exhibits a strength–ductility trade-off because of its coarse lamellar microstructure.
Over-annealing would coarsen the microstructure and eliminate the beneficial effect.
Excessive rolling deformation could induce damage and eliminate the beneficial effect.
The quantitative strength and ductility changes depend on processing conditions, alloy composition, and the scale of microstructural refinement.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis says that both strength and ductility increase, whereas the predicted outcome allows ductility merely to be maintained; the falsification rule again requires a statistically significant increase in both properties.
